back: Describes an activity in progress until recently or the time of speaking.
Verbs like belong, know, and understand are typically not used in the continuous.
Continuous focuses on the process of the activity; simple focuses on the result.
Continuous emphasizes ongoing/repeated activity; simple suggests the activity is finished.
The continuous is often used to complain about something evident (e.g., 'Who's been messing with my papers?').
Both forms can often be used for general characteristics or circumstances.
has been staying (emphasizing a temporary stay).
have been reading (emphasizing the ongoing process).
has given (focusing on the total result).
have been swimming (recent activity with present effect).
has been claiming more than 50,000 lives.
The government has been making massive progress (ongoing).
Prices have been decreasing recently (ongoing trend).
